source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 5 May 1927, p. 11 ("Rural council and guardians: Newtownards nominations")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: Names and divisions read on the block images of the News-Letter's nominations report (5 May 1927, p. 11, article BNL19270505.2.229) and results (4 June 1927, p. 8, article BNL19270604.2.190).

note: Triennial election of the Newtownards (later North Down) rural district councillors, one for each of eighteen divisions; nominations received by Mr. John Warden, deputy returning officer, on 4 May 1927. Ballywalter was the only contest, polled Thursday 2 June 1927 and declared the next day; in Crawfordsburn, Groomsport, Portaferry and Quintin no nomination was received and the retiring members were deemed re-elected. No party labels are printed. Sole nomination (old member); returned unopposed. Division printed 'Donagahadee'. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Donaghadee' to Donaghadee Rural (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Donaghadee Rural; the rounds were filed as Donaghadee (1924, 1927, 1930, 1933, 1946, 1952, 1958); Donaghadee Rural (1939). This round was filed as 'Donaghadee', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (donaghadee) answers with a redirect to this one.
